settings.objective: Safety barrier first; then delay cost + lambda * sector excess aircraft-minutes. Final selection uses native execution.
settings.delay_basis: Fixed departure requested ready-event; arrival uncontrolled touchdown from identical initial state
settings.primary_comparison: Best native FCFS (1-min and 5-min grids) vs TEAM_GROUND; TEAM_MIXED adds arrival speed control

limitations: Synthetic study routes, levels, scheduling and sector limits; not operational procedures.
Capacity is simultaneous airborne occupancy within the displayed study sector, not movements/hour or whole-screen count.
Both cases enforce airborne and runway safety. Only the overload case intentionally exceeds a sector occupancy limit.
Mixed arrival/departure pairs use 5 NM or 1,000 ft when both are within 40 NM and at or below 10,000 ft; Centre and same-direction-pair rules retain 10/20 NM.
Origin-airport transit for arrivals is a timing assumption outside the modelled upstream admission.
Bounded taxi queues, lineup, full runway evacuation, a 6 NM takeoff-roll cutoff, 30 seconds from wheel-off to next touchdown, and arrival parking are included.
Named airway coordinates are saved references; non-network joins are labelled assumed connectors.
All study inputs are synthetic. Feasible_sampled is a model diagnostic, not operational validation.
Search uses native 1 s arrival trajectories and 1 s arrival-pair checks; occupancy and mixed/departure screening use 20 s. Up to four native execution checkpoints per method/seed guide selection.
Only the explicit upstream sector-to-endpoint geometry is replayed; external origin transit is a timing assumption.

Delay uses fixed departure requested ready-events and the uncontrolled arrival touchdown from identical initial airborne states. Additional and signed changes from the reference are reported separately.
FCFS preserves requested readiness order after committed surface traffic; both 1-minute and 5-minute grids are executed and the better native objective is the main comparator.
GA ground vs FCFS compares departure regulation; GA mixed also has Centre speed control. Ten fixed seeds describe search variability, not operational statistical significance.
Native safety metering may extend proposed CTOT holds; withdrawn speed proposals and executed controls are recorded per flight.
